newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Early figures show Argentine jobless rate up - paper.
newsitem.headline: Early figures show Argentine jobless rate up - paper.

text.p: Preliminary results of a regular Argentine government unemployment survey showed that the unemployment rate had risen to between 17.5 percent and 18.1 percent by October, the Clarin newspaper reported Sunday.
The last survey, in May, put unemployment at 17.1 percent.
Early analysis of the October survey showed a jump in unemployment in greater Buenos Aires to 19 percent from 18 percent in May, according to government sources.
The economy minister's chief adviser Carlos Rodriguez confirmed to Clarin that joblessness seemed to have risen in Buenos Aires and other cities.
"Everything indicates that there had been no recovery in demand for workers at the time of carrying out the unemployment survey," he said.
Rodriguez said he thought unemployment would soon begin to fall, but added that he was "cautious" as to how quickly.
The official results of the October survey are due to be released in the next few days.

The government has pinned many of its hopes for reducing joblessness on a package of measures to make working hours more flexible and reduce employers' costs. But so far it has had difficulty getting Congress to approve the laws and President Carlos Menem has threatened to pass them by decree.
